claims.claim: A divorce can be heard in England and Wales if either party to the marriage is domiciled in England and Wales.
claims.quote: either of the parties to the marriage is domiciled in England and Wales
claims.note: Section 5(2)(g) of the Act gives the court jurisdiction where either party is domiciled in England and Wales.

claims.claim: A divorce can be heard in England and Wales if a party has been habitually resident there for at least 6 of the last 12 months.
claims.quote: the applicant is domiciled and habitually resident in England and Wales and has resided there for at least six months immediately before the application was made
claims.note: The six-month residence ground applies only to an applicant who is also domiciled in England and Wales and requires six months immediately before applying; residence alone needs at least one year, and the text has no '6 of the last 12 months' rule.
